v1.feedback: The L-system tree is clearly readable and the Kusama dot-rain concept lands — red polka dots falling through and briefly infecting the canopy is a legit 'surprise swerve' on the parent. Two issues: the burst cycle could be more dramatic — right now the red dots appear and fade so quickly they read as a glitch rather than a deliberate Kusama invasion; consider lengthening the burst hold time and staggering it spatially (bottom-up wave) so the takeover feels intentional. The falling dot rain particles are too sparse and too small at default zoom to register as 'rain' — double DOT_N and increase their gl_PointSize so the polka-dot shower is unmistakable within the first 2 seconds. Palette is restrained and the tree form fills frame well.

v2.feedback: The Kusama infection wave climbing the L-system tree is a legit surprise swerve — the red polka dots colonizing branches bottom-up reads clearly as 'Yayoi meets procedural botany' within 2 seconds. The falling dot-rain is a nice touch but the dots could use slightly more size variation and a gentler fade-in to avoid the uniform-grid feel at the top of frame. Consider tightening the camera start so the tree fills more vertical space on load — right now ~30% of the canvas is empty sky before the rain thickens. The palette restraint is good (bark-green to Kusama-red only), but the additive blending on the red dots washes them toward orange at overlap — try a non-additive pass or clamp the red channel to keep the signature Kusama vermillion punchy.
